problem_motivation.content: First-principles studies of coherent two-phase composites are rare.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: Papers related to first-principles calculations of these two-phase coherent nanocomposites are rather rare as most of the previous studies focused on individual phases

problem_motivation.content: Fe-Al alloys lose ductility and high-temperature strength.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: their wider use is hindered by their low ductility at ambient temperatures and a drop of the strength at elevated temperatures

prior_limitation.content: Common LDA and PBE calculations do not reproduce the observed Fe3Al ground state.
prior_limitation.evidence_span: neither LDA nor PBE parametrization of GGA can correctly reproduce the D0 3 structure as the ground state of Fe 3 Al

causal_claim.content: Lateral stress linearly raises tensile strength.
causal_claim.evidence_span: the tensile strength σ ts for all structures linearly increases with increasing of the lateral stress σ lt
the thermal vibrations significantly decrease the tensile strength

mechanism_principle.content: Softening elastic constants produce mechanical instability before the nominal strength maximum.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: mechanical stability is strongly affected by softening of elastic constants C ′ and/or C 66 and by corresponding elastic instabilities

mechanism_principle.content: The disordered Fe-Al phase is the weak point governing nanocomposite tensile failure.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: the disordered Fe-Al phase represents the weakest point of the studied nanocomposite in terms of tensile loading

evidence_result.content: Heating to 300 K cuts Fe3Al strength to about 12.5 GPa.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the strength decreases from 16.7 GPa (obtained from the T = 1 K simulations) to values approx. 12.5 GPa for temperature 300 K, i.e., only 75 %

evidence_result.content: Under OUL loading, Fe3Al tensile strength is only 4.1 GPa.
evidence_result.evidence_span: the related tensile strength ( σ ts OUL = 4.1 GPa), i.e., only 17 % of the value found in the case of the OUD model

constraint.content: The OUD loading path produces a nearly hydrostatic stress state.
constraint.evidence_span: the uniaxial deformation (OUD) leads to nearly identical values of all three normal stresses, i.e., σ x = σ y = σ ax , means that the loading is almost hydrostatic

constraint.content: Defect-free simulations may overestimate tensile strength.
constraint.evidence_span: we have simulated behavior of defect-free systems while some crystal defects or instabilities might lower the tensile strength

constraint.content: The defect-free calculations may overestimate strength because phonon effects were omitted.
constraint.evidence_span: quantum-mechanical phonon calculations, which can assess temperature effect, are computationally very demanding and, therefore, we leave it for future studies
